summary: The candidate fixes idle RadixCache retention and the happy-path live disaggregated-PREFILL fixture, but sender-cleanup can be skipped for a chunk already present in retract_reqs and an abort exception escapes before the cache/pool release boundary. This is a partial original-issue fix.

tests.what_was_measured: Recorded base failed both candidate regressions: idle radix prefix remained matchable 4/4 and live PREFILL sender teardown was absent.
Exact candidate focused regression suite: 36 passed and 2 subtests passed.

Independent boundary suite: inherited candidate coverage passed, while two adversarial cases failed because sender cleanup was skipped for a live chunk already in running_batch and abort exceptions prevented cache/pool reset.
One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 executed a Torch GPU tensor operation and returned 14.0.

gpu_execution.evidence: Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2 detected one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950); tensor sum-of-squares was 14.0. Issue-specific tests were CPU-side.

remaining_counterexamples: If a live disaggregated-PREFILL chunked_req is already in retract_reqs (for example also represented in running_batch), the candidate's guard skips pending-send cleanup, sender abort, and metadata release, yet retracts the request and resets the cache/pools.
If disagg_kv_sender.abort() raises, pause_generation exits before retract_all and before tree_cache/request-pool/token-allocator reset, so no complete KV-release boundary is established.
remaining_limitations: No Qwen model weights were available; old/new-weight logprob and generated-text divergence were not reproduced.
No multi-node disaggregated deployment was available; live NIXL/Mooncake/MORI transfer cancellation was not validated end to end.
The running_batch/chunked_req overlap was tested as a deterministic scheduler invariant boundary, not observed in a live normal scheduling loop.
No native source changed and repository-environment.json specifies no native artifact, so no native rebuild was applicable.
